page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.1-16 is a flexible virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Compute capacity is delivered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with one dedicated physical core supporting simultaneous multithreading, which yields two virtual CPUs. Because the allocation model is dedicated, compute cycles are not shared with neighboring workloads, avoiding noisy neighbor contention.

The memory allocation totals 16.0 GB, resulting in an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio that aligns with memory-heavy profiles. There are no discrete GPUs installed on this instance. Local storage is not provided, meaning the instance relies entirely on network-attached block storage for operating system images and persistent data persistence. Network connectivity is supported by one complimentary public IPv4 address.

From an efficiency standpoint, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio allows systems to maintain substantial in-memory working sets without requiring unnecessary compute core allocations. However, the lack of local NVMe storage introduces reliance on remote block storage latency and throughput limits for disk-bound operations. This profile fits memory-centric services, lightweight relational databases, in-memory key-value stores, monitoring daemons, and microservices requiring a generous memory footprint with modest processor demand.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.1-16 is a flexible virtual compute instance equipped with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The instance features dedicated CPU allocation with two threads per core, paired with 16.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned. The server provides no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning that all persistent file systems must rely on external cloud block volumes. Network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, this shape offers solid cost efficiency for memory-sensitive environments without the necessity of over-provisioning compute resources. VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.1-16 is well suited for memory-intensive background services, small database instances, in-memory caching nodes, and light enterprise web application hosting.
